creature_families.name: hostile mob (EvAdventure)
creature_families.scale: one tier only; HP = 4 x hit dice; all six abilities equal the hit dice; fixed armour value; morale 7-9 set per NPC
creature_families.signature: per-tick intent table: hold 0, attack 0.85, stunt 0.05, item 0, flee 0.05

creature_families.name: state-machine mob (tutorial world)
creature_families.scale: one tier; health 20; no tier table in the repo
creature_families.signature: idle, patrol, hunt, attack and dead states on one ticker; paces 6 s patrol, 2 s attack, 1 s hunt, 100 s dead

creature_families.name: talkative NPC (immortal)
creature_families.signature: dodges damage with a line and opens a menu on talk

creature_families.name: shopkeeper (immortal)
creature_families.signature: brushes off hits; buys at miser factor 0.5 and sells at upsell factor 1.0 by default

creature_families.name: quest giver
creature_families.signature: talkative NPC that dispenses quests through its menu

top_creatures.label: Morale-gated mob
top_creatures.why: A per-creature morale number and one 2d6 roll would decide whether the creature keeps fighting, a cheap readable fear beat. The donor defines the check but no caller in the contrib invokes it, so the behaviour is a designed idea, not a shipped one.
top_creatures.keep: kept: morale as a per-creature number (7-9) and a single two-dice check against it.
top_creatures.change: changed: wire the check to a real trigger (hurt or ally loss), our own dice, and a break result that sends the creature to a different corner, not just a flee step.

top_creatures.label: One-number stat block
top_creatures.why: One hit-dice value sets HP, to-hit and every ability, so a creature is authored with one number and reads as tougher or weaker at a glance.
top_creatures.keep: kept: one number drives HP (4 x value) and the defence bonus.
top_creatures.change: changed: separate HP, damage and speed per creature family; no shared ability block.

top_creatures.label: Four-state patrol mob
top_creatures.why: Slow wandering, fast attacking and fastest hunting on one ticker reads as a creature mood, and each state is a separate pace value a designer can tune.
top_creatures.keep: kept: one ticker per state, pace stored per state (patrol 6 s, attack 2 s, hunt 1 s, dead 100 s).
top_creatures.change: changed: our own paces per family, and the hunt ticker must name the real method (the donor names do_hunt but defines do_hunting).

top_creatures.label: Intent table as personality
top_creatures.why: Each tick a creature rolls one intent from a weighted table, so the same species can feel aggressive or cautious just by changing weights.
top_creatures.keep: kept: a weighted table of hold, attack, stunt, flee as the creature's personality.
top_creatures.change: changed: intent sets per family (a pack creature stunts allies more); our own weights; the attack arm has to match the key (donor's arm is named combat).

top_creatures.label: Look-around idle line
top_creatures.why: A rare idle line (about 1 in 100 ticks) gives a standing creature life without any extra animation budget.
top_creatures.keep: kept: rare idle text on a tick roll, only when nothing else happens.
top_creatures.change: changed: idle clip variants per family instead of text, and a per-family rate.

top_creatures.label: Flee away from the way you came
top_creatures.why: A fleeing creature never doubles back into the room it just left, so the chase reads as running, not dancing.
top_creatures.keep: kept: exclude the previous room from flee exits; fall back to roam in a dead end.
top_creatures.change: changed: flee toward a home point or a safe zone rather than any exit; our own dead-end rule.

top_creatures.label: Magic gate on armour
top_creatures.why: Ordinary weapons barely scratch a tough creature (damage divided by 100 unless the weapon is magic), so the player has to find the right tool; that is a clear, teachable gate.
top_creatures.keep: kept: a damage gate per creature that a weapon class must pass.
top_creatures.change: changed: resistance per family rather than one global number; a visible cue on a glancing hit.

top_creatures.label: Timed return after death
top_creatures.why: A mob's body stays on the ground for a fixed time, then the creature returns at full health; players get a pause and a reset rather than a lingering corpse.
top_creatures.keep: kept: a death state with its own timer and a full-health return.
top_creatures.change: changed: our own death presentation and return rule (for example a spawn point on a timer tied to the zone).

classes.name: classless knave (the only character type)
classes.role: one character build; role comes from weapons, armour and spells chosen at creation
classes.mechanic: six abilities from the lowest of three d6; three rune-stone spells carried as items
classes.progression: XP threshold 1000 x level; level-up adds one to up to three abilities, capped at 10; HP re-roll on level-up has a defect (reads max_hp, which is not defined)

classes.name: races and named factions
classes.mechanic: NPC allegiance is a three-state value: hostile, neutral, friendly

weapon_families.damage: 1d6 by default; a critical hit rolls the damage twice and adds
weapon_families.special: critical miss costs one quality point; quality 0 means broken and unusable
is a weapon and a consumable at once (tag tuple)
one use; refreshed by resting, not deleted after use
singleton with quality None; never breaks

gear_tiers.tier: armour: body base value, shield and helmet as bonuses
gear_tiers.how_shown: armour total in the text sheet only; no visual tier in the repo

gear_tiers.tier: treasure tag on a worn item (example: golden helmet = helmet plus treasure)
gear_tiers.how_shown: two type tags on one object: wear slot and sell value

zones.name: dungeon entrance hub
zones.archetype: start room whose exits each open a separate branch
zones.rules: each exit is re-armed with a 50 percent roll on a 5-minute tick; a branch collapses after a week without a new room

zones.name: generated dungeon rooms
zones.archetype: grid rooms made on first entry; radial depth from the entrance picks a name tier from 1 to 10, deeper rooms fall back to dark rooms
zones.rules: a branch-wide budget: a new room opens up to two unexplored exits while fewer than two are open; the room stays blocked until a not_clear tag is removed

zones.name: non-lethal PvP arena
zones.archetype: room flag set so players can fight without death
zones.rules: allow_pvp and allow_combat true; losers are knocked out, not killed

zones.name: weather outdoor room
zones.rules: tick every 50 to 70 seconds; a weather line on 20 percent of ticks

zones.name: unsafe bridge
zones.archetype: one room that acts as five positions
zones.rules: steps move a counter from 0 to 4; a fall check on look at the west and centre positions only, 5 percent

zones.name: dark room
zones.archetype: room with no light until a light source is carried
zones.rules: search up to four times, each try 90 percent nothing found, then the find branch runs

zones.name: teleport room and intro and outro rooms
zones.rules: class lines only read; behaviour not read

zones.name: dungeon collapse
zones.archetype: forced return when a branch expires
zones.rules: every character in the branch is moved to the start room with a message; the branch and its rooms are deleted (room deletion is defective, see notes)

looks.label: Room mini-map from exits
looks.technique: a small grid built from the room's exits: a centre mark for the player, a symbol per cardinal exit, a second mark for a room beyond; non-cardinal exits show a different centre mark; hidden for screen-reader users

looks.label: Health as words
looks.technique: health percent is bucketed into eight coloured text labels from Perfect to Collapsed; readable at phone width without a bar

looks.label: Blocked-path footer
looks.technique: a status line appended to the room text in red while an exit is locked, and removed when the room is cleared

looks.label: Non-lethal PvP footer
looks.technique: a yellow footer that states the rule of the room in one line

looks.label: Dark room light gating
looks.technique: room lit flag plus a carried light source; without light the view and search are reduced to messages

looks.label: Ambient idle lines
looks.technique: rare text on a tick roll for creatures (1 in 100) and weather (1 in 5) so an empty room still moves

originals.name: Doorway branch
originals.idea: Each entrance door opens a private branch on first use; anyone who takes the same door inside a short window joins that branch. Branches collapse after a quiet spell and send everyone back to the hub with a message.
originals.keep: kept: rooms generated on first entry; a shared branch for people who take the same door; a collapse that returns players to the hub.
originals.change: changed: the window is per party, not per door; our own theme and room grammar; a collapse that keeps loot rather than only moving people. Fix the defect: the branch timer must refresh when anyone walks a known room, not only when a new room is made.

originals.name: Spell as carried item
originals.idea: A spell is an item in a hand slot with one use; resting refreshes it, so magic is something you carry and plan around.
originals.keep: kept: the spell is an item, two-handed, refreshed by resting, not destroyed on use.
originals.change: changed: refresh per room or per kill instead of per rest; our own carrier (a glyph or a charm), and a visible charge state on the model.

originals.name: Load that slows the hand
originals.idea: Carrying capacity is a number of slots; effects such as mud fill slots and make items there unusable until cleaned.
originals.keep: kept: a fixed slot budget and an effect that fills slots.
originals.change: changed: slot pressure lowers attack timing or stance rather than only blocking items; our own filler effects; fix the defect that the filler's type tag is set to a string and fails on creation.

originals.name: Depth-tiered rooms
originals.idea: Distance from the entrance sets the room tier; the tier names the rooms and sets how hard the room is, so depth is the difficulty dial.
originals.keep: kept: radial depth from the entrance as the difficulty input; ten named tiers then a fallback.
originals.change: changed: our own biome sets and tier rules; difficulty from spawn tables, not names alone.

originals.name: Five-step bridge
originals.idea: A hazardous crossing is one place with five positions; each step moves a counter and the risk is tied to the middle positions.
originals.keep: kept: a short position counter and a risk band in the middle.
originals.change: changed: the risk rolls on each step, not on looking around (the donor rolls on look, which lets a player avoid the risk by not looking); our own hazard and our own ends.

originals.name: Morale break
originals.idea: A creature checks its morale at a set trigger; a failed check breaks it off to a corner instead of fighting on. The donor has the check (rules.py) and the morale value (npcs.py) but no caller, so the trigger is ours to design.
originals.keep: kept: per-creature morale and a two-dice check.
originals.change: changed: our own trigger and break behaviour (a retreat to a home point, a call to allies); morale set per family.

originals.name: Death roll with lasting scars
originals.idea: Reaching zero health rolls on a table: most results leave the character alive with one ability lowered for good and a small heal; a few kill.
originals.keep: kept: a single roll at zero health; mostly-survive outcomes with a permanent cost.
originals.change: changed: the cost lasts until a shrine visit or a fight, not forever; our own list of costs; the death chance and the stat list are ours.

originals.name: Non-lethal arena
originals.idea: A duel room where a loser is knocked out and restored, not killed; the footer states the rule.
originals.keep: kept: a flag per room for lethal and non-lethal fighting; one-line rule footer.
originals.change: changed: our own knock-out rule and a reward split for the winner.
